transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, I came in because... I just feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore. It's like I have to jump up and do the next thing, even when I'm completely worn out and I really should just be sitting still. I tried to sit in my recliner yesterday to rest—it’s this lovely blue chair I got on sale at Macy's years ago, back when they actually had good sales, you know? The quality of furniture these days is just terrible, everything is made of that cheap particle board. My sister bought a coffee table last month and the leg snapped right off the very first day! She was so mad she drove it right back to the store in her trunk and made them give her a refund in cash. But... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. I was trying to sit in my chair, and I just couldn't. I'm so tired, but my body just makes me get up and find something else to do.
Have you recently started any new medications or had a dose changed?

No, no new pills. Everything is exactly the same as it's been. I just get my regular refills at the CVS down on Main Street. Although, I've really been thinking about switching pharmacies because the line at the drive-thru is always wrapped all the way around the building. Last time I went, I was sitting behind this silver Honda for twenty minutes! The woman driving was just chatting away with the pharmacist through the window like they were at a coffee shop. 

Which reminds me, I really miss when pharmacies had those little soda fountains in them. When I was a little girl, my grandmother used to take me to the Rexall drug store and buy me a cherry vanilla float. You just can't find ice cream like that anymore. Everything now is all artificial flavors and high fructose corn syrup. It's no wonder everyone's stomach is always upset these days, nobody eats real food. I try to buy organic when I can, but the prices at the grocery store are just outrageous. A carton of eggs is practically the price of a steak! 

But... oh, what were you asking me? Did I change my medicine? No, no, it's all the same.

Depressed? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm not really a down-in-the-dumps kind of person. I do get a little sad when I watch the evening news sometimes, though. The news is just so terrible lately, isn't it? My neighbor, Margaret, she watches those 24-hour news channels all day long and she is just miserable all the time. I told her she needs to turn that television off and go plant some petunias or something. Gardening is so good for you. 

I tried to grow beefsteak tomatoes last summer, but the squirrels kept taking exactly one bite out of the green ones and leaving them sitting on the fence! They are such a nuisance. I went down to the hardware store to buy some of that chicken wire to keep them out, but the boy working in the garden center had no idea where anything was. He was just a teenager, probably his very first job, poor thing. Kids these days just don't get trained properly at all. Management just hands them an apron and says good luck. It's a shame, really. 

But... oh dear, I lost my train of thought again. What did you ask me? Was I depressed? No, no, I've never felt deeply down for weeks at a time or anything like that. Just this awful restless feeling I told you about.

High energy? Like I said, I just can't settle down right now, but before this... no, I don't think I've ever felt this way before. It's so strange, honestly. Usually I'm perfectly happy just knitting on the porch. I make these little baby blankets for the hospital downtown. They take donations for the NICU, you know. I started doing it after my niece had her twins—oh, they were so tiny, like little dolls! They're in middle school now, which just blows my mind. The boy, Tommy, he's playing the trumpet in the school band. My sister says it sounds like a dying goose when he practices, but you have to encourage them, right? Arts in schools are the first thing to get their funding cut when the city budget gets tight. They just built a new football stadium though, millions of dollars for a high school stadium! The priorities in this town are just completely backwards if you ask me. We need better roads, not astroturf. There's a pothole on Elm Street that nearly took off my hubcap last Tuesday. 

Wait, what were we talking about? High energy? No, just this current feeling of needing to jump out of my skin. Never before this.
Has this restless energy caused severe problems with managing your daily chores, work, or relationships?

Well, yes, it really has caused some problems lately. It's actually been quite embarrassing for me. My daughter had to come over and take my checkbook away because I completely messed up the electric bill and the water bill. I just couldn't sit still long enough to balance it out. She works at the bank, you know, the one with the big green sign over by the highway. She’s a loan officer. She always tells me that people don't read the fine print on their mortgages anymore. They just sign away without looking at the interest rates! I remember when my husband and I bought our first house, the interest rates were sky high, but we managed. We had this beautiful oak tree in the front yard that turned the most brilliant shade of red in the autumn. 

Oh, I love autumn. The crisp air, the apple cider. We used to go to the orchard every October. But the orchard we used to go to got sold to a developer, and now it's just a bunch of townhouses that all look exactly the same. Beige siding, beige doors. No character at all! It's such a shame how they're tearing down all the beautiful old farms around here. 

But, oh, I'm sorry, you were asking about my chores and things? Yes, it's been awful. At church, they had to find someone else to organize the bake sale because I just kept forgetting who was bringing the brownies and who was bringing the pies. And the ladies at the community garden had to completely redo the planting schedule I was supposed to make. I just dropped the ball on all of it. I feel terrible because the groups I care about just don't feel like they can count on me right now.
